newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria may give up building nuclear waste storage facility.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria may give up building nuclear waste storage facility.

text.p: Bulgaria may give up building its own storage facility for highly radioactive spent fuel if next week Russia agrees to dispose it from all the six Soviet-made reactors at Kozloduy, former energy minister said on Thursday.

Roumen Ovcharov, who is to hand over his post later on Thursday to his successor from the new interim government Georgi Stoilov, said senior Russian officials were expected to visit Sofia next week to discuss the disposal of spent fuel from the Kozloduy nuclear power plant.
"If Russia agrees to dispose our spent fuel, we will give up the tender we announced last year for a technological project to plan the dry waste storage facility," Ovcharov told reporters.
Bids from three firms are being considered for the project to plan the storage facility, which will hold spent fuel for up to 50 years.
In the past, the Soviet Union reprocessed and disposed of spent fuel from the Kozloduy plant without charge under a bilateral agreement which expired in 1990.

The spent fuel has since been left unprocessed in a temporary storage at Kozloduy. Moscow adopted a law on environmental protection in 1992 which banned the shipment of nuclear waste to its territory.
The 3,760-megawatt Kozloduy plant meets more than 40 percent of Bulgaria's fuel needs.
